module.title: Task System
module.description:
Tasks are first-class items that track work. They can be derived
from spec items or created standalone. The task system enables
kspec to function as a work tracker, not just a spec format.

items.title: Task Types
items.description:
Tasks have types that indicate their nature and relationship
to spec items. Some types expect spec linkage; others don't.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is created or derived
acceptance_criteria.then: the type is stored as one of the supported task classifications: task, epic, bug, spike, or infra

items.title: State - pending
items.description:
status: pending

Initial state. Work not yet started.
Transitions: start -> in_progress, cancel -> cancelled

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has status pending
acceptance_criteria.when: a user runs kspec task start or kspec task cancel
acceptance_criteria.then: the task transitions to in_progress or cancelled respectively

items.title: State - in_progress
items.description:
status: in_progress

Work actively being done.
Transitions:
- complete -> completed
- block -> blocked
- cancel -> cancelled

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has status in_progress
acceptance_criteria.when: a user runs kspec task submit, kspec task block, or kspec task cancel
acceptance_criteria.then: the task transitions to pending_review, blocked, or cancelled respectively

items.title: State - blocked
items.description:
status: blocked

Work paused due to blocker.
Can be set manually (external blocker) or auto-computed
when depends_on items aren't completed.

Transitions: unblock -> in_progress (or pending)

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has status blocked
acceptance_criteria.when: the blocker is cleared and the task is unblocked
acceptance_criteria.then: the task returns to pending or in_progress instead of transitioning directly to a terminal state

items.title: State - completed
items.description:
status: completed

Work finished successfully. Terminal state.
Should include closed_reason describing outcome.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is marked completed
acceptance_criteria.then: the task remains in the terminal completed state and stores a closed_reason describing the outcome

items.title: State - cancelled
items.description:
status: cancelled

Work abandoned. Terminal state.
Should include closed_reason explaining why.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is cancelled
acceptance_criteria.then: the task remains in the terminal cancelled state and stores a closed_reason explaining why work stopped

items.title: Derived State - ready
items.description:
"ready" is a computed view, not stored state:
ready = (pending OR needs_work) + all depends_on completed + no blockers

`kspec tasks ready` returns tasks in this state.
This is the primary query for "what can I work on?"

needs_work tasks are sorted before pending — fix cycles take priority.

acceptance_criteria.given: tasks exist in pending, needs_work, blocked, and unmet-dependency states
acceptance_criteria.then: only pending or needs_work tasks with completed dependencies and no blockers are returned, with needs_work tasks listed before pending tasks

items.title: Task Schema
items.description:
Tasks are items with additional fields for work tracking.
Key principle: don't duplicate spec content, reference it.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task implements a spec item
acceptance_criteria.then: the task keeps execution metadata plus a spec_ref link instead of duplicating the linked spec's description and acceptance criteria

items.title: Spec Reference Field
items.description:
spec_ref: "@feature-slug"

Links task to the spec item it implements.
The spec item has the full description, acceptance
criteria, etc. Task adds only execution metadata.

Optional for free-form tasks (bug, infra).

acceptance_criteria.given: a task implements a spec item or represents free-form work
acceptance_criteria.then: spec_ref points to the linked spec item when present and may be omitted for free-form bug or infra tasks

items.title: Work Metadata Fields
items.description:
Task-specific fields for work tracking:

- priority: 1-5 (1 highest) or high/medium/low
- complexity: Relative size estimate (fibonacci or 1-5)
- assignee: Who's working on it (optional)
- blocked_by: Manual blockers (strings, not refs)
- closed_reason: Why completed/cancelled

These fields don't exist on regular spec items.

acceptance_criteria.given: task-specific metadata is present
acceptance_criteria.then: priority, complexity, assignee, blocked_by, and closed_reason are accepted on tasks without becoming required fields on regular spec items

items.title: Task Timestamps
items.description:
Auto-populated timestamps:

- created_at: When task was created
- started_at: When status became in_progress
- completed_at: When status became completed/cancelled

Format: ISO 8601 (2025-01-14T10:00:00Z)

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is created, started, or completed or cancelled
acceptance_criteria.when: task lifecycle commands persist the change
acceptance_criteria.then: created_at, started_at, and completed_at are auto-populated as ISO 8601 timestamps at the matching lifecycle transition

items.title: VCS References
items.description:
vcs_refs links tasks to git branches/commits/tags:

vcs_refs:
  - ref: "feat/user-login"
    type: branch
  - ref: "abc123"
    type: commit

Minimal schema, extensible as needed.

acceptance_criteria.given: vcs_refs are attached to a task
acceptance_criteria.then: each vcs_refs entry stores a git reference string and a type such as branch, commit, or tag

items.title: Derive Command
items.description:
kspec derive <ref>     # Derive task for single item
kspec derive --all    # Derive for all items without tasks

Creates task with:
- title: "Implement <item title>" (adjustable)
- type: task (or epic for features with children)
- spec_ref: @<item>
- derivation: auto

acceptance_criteria.given: a user runs kspec derive @item or kspec derive --all
acceptance_criteria.when: derivation creates work for an uncovered item
acceptance_criteria.then: the created task includes a derived title, task type, spec_ref, and derivation metadata

items.title: Derivation Idempotency
items.description:
Derivation is idempotent:
- If task with spec_ref to item exists, skip creation
- Use --force to create additional task anyway
- Useful for re-running derive without duplicates

acceptance_criteria.given: a task already exists for an item's spec_ref
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec derive is run again without --force
acceptance_criteria.then: no duplicate task is created for that spec item

items.title: Note Structure
items.description:
Note entries have:
- _ulid: Entry identifier
- created_at: Timestamp
- author: Who added it
- content: The note text (multiline)
- supersedes: ULID of entry this corrects (optional)

Notes are never deleted, only superseded.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note is added to a task
acceptance_criteria.then: the entry records its ULID, created_at timestamp, author, content, and optional supersedes reference while preserving earlier notes

items.title: Note CLI Commands
items.description:
kspec task note <ref> "message"      # Add note
kspec task note <ref> --supersedes <id> "correction"
kspec task notes <ref>               # Show notes log

JSON output available for all commands.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user runs kspec task note @task "message" or kspec task notes @task
acceptance_criteria.then: the note is appended to the task log and the notes command returns the append-only note history

items.title: Todo Structure
items.description:
Todo entries have:
- id: Local numeric ID (within task)
- text: The todo description
- done: Boolean
- done_at: When marked done (if done)
- added_at: When created
- added_by: Who added it
- promoted_to: @ref if promoted to task (optional)

acceptance_criteria.given: a todo is added to a task and later marked done or not done
acceptance_criteria.then: it records a local id, text, done state, timestamps, author, and keeps the same identity across later status changes

items.title: Todo CLI Commands
items.description:
kspec todo add <ref> "text"     # Add todo
kspec todo done <ref> <id>      # Mark complete
kspec todo promote <ref> <id>   # Promote to task
kspec task todos <ref>          # List todos

Todos are for quick capture; promote when complex.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user runs kspec task todo add, kspec task todo done, kspec task todo undone, or kspec task todos
acceptance_criteria.then: the task todo list is updated and the current todo entries can be listed from the task

items.title: Task Storage
items.description:
Tasks are stored alongside or separate from specs.
Auto-adaptive: start alongside, separate when volume grows.

acceptance_criteria.given: a project uses the task system
acceptance_criteria.then: the system supports storing them either alongside module specs or in a dedicated tasks directory without changing task semantics

items.title: Storage - Alongside Specs
items.description:
For smaller projects, tasks next to specs:

spec/
  auth.yaml           # Spec items
  auth.tasks.yaml     # Tasks for auth module

Simple, keeps related items together.

acceptance_criteria.given: a smaller project stores tasks alongside specs
acceptance_criteria.when: a module has a companion .tasks.yaml file next to its spec file
acceptance_criteria.then: tasks for that module remain colocated with the related spec

items.title: Storage - Separate Directory
items.description:
For larger projects, separate tasks directory:

spec/
  modules/
    auth.yaml
tasks/
  backlog.yaml
  active.yaml
  archive/
    2025-01.yaml

Separates concerns, enables archiving.

acceptance_criteria.given: a larger project uses separate task storage
acceptance_criteria.when: tasks are persisted under tasks backlog, active, or archive files
acceptance_criteria.then: task data is stored separately from module spec files and can be archived independently

items.title: Ready Tasks Query
items.description:
kspec tasks ready

Returns tasks where:
- status = pending OR needs_work
- all depends_on tasks are completed
- no manual blocked_by entries
- sorted: needs_work first, then pending (fix cycles take priority)

This is THE command for "what can I work on next?"

acceptance_criteria.given: tasks have mixed statuses, blockers, and dependencies
acceptance_criteria.then: it returns only ready tasks and orders needs_work ahead of pending

items.title: Next Task Query
items.description:
kspec tasks next

Returns single highest-priority ready task.
Sorting: priority (asc) -> created_at (asc)

Useful for agents: "give me one thing to do"

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple ready tasks exist
acceptance_criteria.then: it returns the single ready task with the highest priority, breaking ties by oldest created_at first

items.title: Task Query Filters
items.description:
kspec tasks list [filters]

Filters:
- --status <state>    # By status
- --type <type>       # By task type
- --tag <tag>         # By tag
- --assignee <who>    # By assignee
- --spec-ref <ref>    # By linked spec item

All queries support --json output.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user runs kspec tasks list with --status, --type, --tag, or --meta-ref and optionally --json
acceptance_criteria.then: only matching tasks are returned and JSON output remains available for the filtered result set
